triggers.query: Write a seeded generative soundtrack for my web app with Web Audio.
I want a generative drum and bass track for my game. I do not know the style well. Where do I start?
My generated lo-fi loop gets annoying after ten minutes and the hats are piercing. How do I fix it?
Add a dreamy space-themed track to my game's procedural music system.
Compose a melody and chord progression for my song in C minor.
Master and EQ my recorded podcast so the voice is clearer.
Write a prompt for Suno to make a lo-fi beat.

behavior.task: I need a generative track in a style I do not know well: 1990s bossa-nova-flavoured lounge music for a hotel app. Describe exactly how you would go about learning the style and what you would produce before writing any code.
assert: Researches the style on the web from more than one angle (tutorials, theory or education pages, history or gear, analyses of real tracks, listener or forum views) rather than relying on memory
Produces a written style sheet or spec with fields such as tempo, harmony, rhythm patterns, voices, form and mix, and what the style's defining traits are
Cross-checks each defining trait against at least two independent sources and marks guesses or unknowns
Notices that numbers from different sources may use different scales or conventions, or are conventions rather than facts
Plans to build to the sheet and verify by measurement and listening, not only by listening

behavior.task: A generated ambient track uses soft bell notes. A listener says a high-pitched tone starts to bother them after a few minutes. Say what you would check and change, in order.
assert: Measures the output (level and the share of energy above about 2 kHz) before changing anything
Lowers the register of the loudest sustained or bell voice, or its upper partial, before touching the notes or harmony
Adds or lowers a voice or master low-pass and darkens the echo or reverb return as a later step
Changes one thing per round and measures again

behavior.task: I am not a composer. My generated synthwave-style driving track loops badly and something in the background sounds weird: the bass pattern and arpeggio change randomly each bar and the drums drop out when the piece restarts. How should the track be built so it loops well and still has a hook?
assert: Locks the bass and arp riff on the grid, varying only at phrase ends (a fill or turnaround bar) and section changes, not randomly per bar
Names the riff or a short lead motif as the hook and has it return with one change
Keeps a pulse (kick, bass or pad) running across the loop join so there is no dropout, with loop lengths in whole bars
Explains terms in plain language for a non-musician
Suggests a measurable check, such as a test that the groove is identical across bars

behavior.task: Design the composer for an endless calm ambient track for a web app that plays for hours, replays from a seed and gets denser and brighter when the app is busy. Give the architecture, how you learn what the style needs, the layers, and how you check it.
assert: Uses a seeded generator and draws the same number of random values whatever the app state is
Derives its choices from a researched or stated style spec rather than asserting values from memory
Chooses its variation mechanism to suit the style (for example independent layers for a texture, locked patterns with phrase-end changes for a groove)
Verifies with tests and a measurement of level and spectrum
